title: Temple B’nai Abraham Religious School
subtitle: Washington, D.C. · March 8–10, 2027
bodyHtml:
Families are currently viewing Temple B’nai Abraham Religious School’s sample itinerary. This version provides a general overview of the experiences and activities the trip organizers hope to include. As departure nears, the school or designated trip organizer will share the most up-to-date and finalized itinerary, reflecting any adjustments, confirmed reservations, and timing updates.

Day 1: The Capital Jewish Museum & the Holocaust Memorial Museum

  • Depart for Washington, D.C.
  • Arrival in Washington, D.C. — meet your Landmark Tour Leader
  • Lunch at Ronald Reagan Building - Meal Voucher
  • Guided tour of the Capital Jewish Museum
  • Free time on the National Mall
  • Visit the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
  • Group sit down dinner
  • Reflection in the hotel meeting room
  • Return to hotel accommodations with overnight security (two nights)

Day 2: African American History, the National Zoo & the Memorials

  • Breakfast included with hotel
  • Visit the National Museum of African American History and Culture
  • Lunch break
  • Visit the Smithsonian National Zoological Park
  • Dinner Allocation
  • Jewish scavenger hunt during the monument tour
  • Guided walking tour of the Lincoln Memorial, Vietnam and Korean War Memorials, World War II Memorial, and Washington Monument
  • Reflection time in the hotel meeting room
  • Return to hotel accommodations

Day 3: Capitol Hill, the Supreme Court & Georgetown

  • Breakfast included with hotel
  • Public guided tour of the United States Capitol Building
  • Meet and greet with a Representative or Senator at Capitol Hill
  • Visit the Supreme Court Building Exhibit
  • Capitol Cafe - Premium Meal Voucher
  • Group exploration of the Georgetown neighborhood
  • Dinner Allocation
  • Depart for home
introHeading: Temple B’nai Abraham Religious School, get ready for an unforgettable Washington, D.C. adventure in 2027! 🏛️
introText: From the galleries of the Capital Jewish Museum to the marble steps of the United States Capitol, this trip brings American history and Jewish heritage to life at every turn. Students will tour the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, take a guided tour of the Capitol and meet with a Representative or Senator, explore the National Museum of African American History and Culture and the National Zoo, and walk the memorials of the National Mall by night. It’s the perfect blend of education, exploration, and fun—an experience your students will be talking about long after the trip ends.
